provenance: All numbers measured in this repository on an RTX 5070 Ti Laptop (sm_120), torch 2.11.0+cu128, 24 logical cores. Transfer figures are 200 episodes per point, seed 42.

pipeline_fixes.note: Complete-success rate on 100 seeded episodes, gnn_k3, before and after the data-pipeline corrections.

bugs.name: Recorded rollouts skipped the expert's first action
bugs.detail: 1 of 30 replayed steps matched the CBS schedule; unshifted matches 31 of 31.

bugs.name: Only the first 5 of ~31 timesteps used
bugs.detail: Policy never observed an agent approaching a goal.

bugs.name: States and actions offset by one
bugs.detail: Trained to predict the action that produced the state.

bugs.name: 80% of samples unreachable
bugs.detail: __len__ returned case count, not sample count.

bugs.name: Self-loops double counted in training only
bugs.detail: Training graphs had 2 on the diagonal, evaluation 1.

transfer_matched_density.note: Board grows as sqrt(agents) so agents-per-cell stays fixed. Horizon 300 steps. Fraction of agents reaching goal.

transfer_fixed_board.note: Board held at 28x28, so adding agents also crowds them. Horizon 42.

training_fleet_size.note: Does training on more agents help? Matched-density evaluation, horizon 300, message-passing model.

horizon_artifact.note: A fixed 42-step horizon on a growing board scores agents on goals they cannot physically reach.

cbs_optimisation.note: Mean seconds per instance, 20 agents on 14x14, 5 instances, identical solve/fail outcomes at every step.

cbs_tail.note: 10 agents on 28x28, 60 instances. Difficulty is long tailed, so a time limit buys most of the speed for a few percent of the cases.

cbs_scaling.note: Instances solved out of 12 on a 28x28 board with 8 obstacles.

rollout_speedup.note: Identical episodes through both paths; results matched exactly every time.

forward_pass.note: Per-forward milliseconds. The model is latency bound, not compute bound, until the batch gets large.
forward_pass.cuda_graph_note: Capturing the forward in a CUDA graph gives 5.2x at 100 episodes (0.594 -> 0.114 ms) but only 1.1x at 1000 (0.776 -> 0.685 ms), because by then the GPU is doing real work.
